policy_description: How Vivida handles local files and update checks, plus general terms of use for the Windows image browser.
policy_intro: Your pictures stay yours. Here is what the app stores locally, when it contacts GitHub, and the general terms for using Vivida.
privacy_local: Vivida opens and decodes images on your device. It does not require an account or include app telemetry, advertising trackers, or a feature that uploads your photos, filenames, or folder contents to Vivida servers. Your last folder, favorite folder paths, language, sort order, grid size, and sidebar preference are saved locally in %APPDATA%\Vivida\state.txt. To clear these preferences, close Vivida and remove that file; uninstalling the app intentionally leaves it in place.
privacy_map: When you open the photo map, Vivida reads location metadata from photos in the current folder on your device and requests visible map tiles and source metadata from tiles.openfreemap.org over HTTPS. It does not send photo files, filenames, or GPS metadata as separate uploads, but the tile coordinates reveal the areas being viewed; OpenFreeMap and any configured proxy can see normal connection information. Map connection mode, the map cache limit (300 MB by default), and a manual proxy address (if used, without credentials) are saved in %APPDATA%\Vivida\state.txt. Map tiles and source metadata are cached under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Vivida\MapTiles. Settings → Map can limit saved tile bytes; source metadata and temporary files are not counted, and evicted tiles may be downloaded again. The old %LOCALAPPDATA%\CUI\MapTiles cache is not moved or deleted automatically. To clear either cache, close Vivida and delete its MapTiles folder manually. OpenFreeMap's terms and privacy practices apply to its service.
privacy_update: On Windows, about one minute after launch, Vivida requests the latest public release from api.github.com over HTTPS. You can also check manually in Settings → About. The request identifies the app version; GitHub receives normal connection details such as your IP address. Neither your photos nor the saved settings file are sent. Vivida does not install updates automatically.
privacy_web: The Vivida application does not include telemetry scripts. An explicit language choice may be saved in your browser's localStorage. GitHub Pages hosts this site, and GitHub serves the downloads and issue tracker. Those services may process normal request data under their own policies; we do not control their log retention.
privacy_contact: For non-sensitive questions, use our public issue tracker. Do not post private photos, personal information, or sensitive file paths in a public issue.
terms_scope: Vivida is a local image browser. Use it in compliance with applicable law and respect other people's rights when viewing, renaming, or deleting files. The app does not grant rights to images you do not own.
terms_services: Update information and downloads are provided through GitHub. External services have their own terms and policies. Installing an update is your choice; the installer does not silently change file associations.
terms_availability: Vivida is provided as available, without a promise that it will always be error-free or suitable for every file. Keep backups of important files before renaming or deleting them. Nothing here limits rights or protections that cannot be waived under applicable law.
terms_changes: These general terms may be revised as the product changes. The date below identifies the version of this page; review the current text when you return.
legal_review: General information only; please obtain legal review before relying on these terms as a legal document.
guide_description: Learn to open folders, save favorite folders, browse photos on a map, use keyboard shortcuts, and configure Vivida on Windows.
guide_intro: A quick tour of folders, favorites, the photo map, viewing, and the shortcuts that make browsing feel natural.
guide_start: Install the Windows 64-bit app for your user account and launch Vivida. Use Places or This PC in the sidebar to navigate; click a folder to enter it or a picture to preview it. You can also start vivida.exe with a folder or picture path as an argument. The installer does not set default image apps for you.
guide_fav: Open the folder you want to keep. In the grid toolbar, click the star next to the sort menu. A filled star means the current folder is saved under Favorites in the left sidebar. Click that folder there to return, or click the star again to remove it. Favorites are folders, not individual pictures; the panel button can show or hide the sidebar.
guide_grid: Choose name, modified date, or size from the sort menu. Scroll with the wheel or the scrollbar. Hold Ctrl while scrolling to change thumbnail size. Thumbnails load progressively as you browse.
guide_viewer: Click a thumbnail to preview it. Zoom with the wheel around your pointer, drag to pan, or double-click to switch between fit and actual pixels. Rotating with R or Shift+R changes only the current display, never the original file.
guide_map: From a folder, switch between the photo grid and Map with the toolbar button. Vivida reads GPS data only from photos in the current folder, so pictures without a location are not marked. Nearby photos gather into one marker. A marker that can be split zooms the map; otherwise it shows a preview, and opening the photo uses the existing viewer. Previous and next move only between photos that have a location. Going up from Map, with the toolbar or Backspace, returns to the grid in the parent folder. Settings → Map selects the Windows proxy, a direct connection, or one HTTP proxy (host:port; no account or SOCKS5) and sets the tile cache from 100 to 2000 MB in steps of 50 MB, with 300 MB as the default. Tiles are stored in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Vivida\MapTiles. An older cache in %LOCALAPPDATA%\CUI\MapTiles is not moved or deleted. If tiles do not load, use Retry. Basemap: OpenFreeMap © OpenMapTiles Data from OpenStreetMap.
guide_settings: Settings → Language changes the interface language. Settings → File Associations lets you explicitly register selected formats; Windows Settings decides actual defaults. Settings → About can check for updates. The unsigned installer may trigger a Windows SmartScreen warning.
grid_move: Move selection and reveal it in the grid
grid_open: Open the selected folder or picture
grid_delete: Confirm deletion to the Recycle Bin
viewer_zoom: Zoom in / out; fit / actual pixels when the viewer has focus
viewer_exit: Leave fullscreen first, then return to grid / return to grid
